description: Plan v7 section 8.3 fixture family 'lvariant-attempted-chain'. Inputs only; the oracle emits expected.

cases.notes: The DUPLICATE refusal of TranslationResult.java:118-122. The chain for en_US_POSIX ends with a variant-lowercased en_US_posix whose toLanguageTag collides case-insensitively with the first candidate's, and the walk only reaches it because no catalog serves first. Paired with lvariant.early-serve.en-us-posix.*, which asks the SAME tag of a fixture that serves at 'en'.

The WELL-FORMEDNESS refusal of LocaleUtils.requireWellFormed via TranslationResult.java:115. Java's own compatibility-extension synthesis produces a Locale that Locale.Builder then rejects; note the offending candidate is the variant-LOWERCASED one, not the legacy ja_JP_JP form, which Locale.Builder.setLocale accepts by special case. Paired with lvariant.early-serve.ja-jp.*.
The th mirror of the ja row, and it is not decoration: it carries the -u-nu- extension rather than -u-ca-, so a port that special-cased one calendar keyword would still refuse this one.

CONTROL. The fourth legacy lvariant shape, on the same fixture as the three refusals: Locale.forLanguageTag folds it to nn-NO, the Norwegian bridge serves the nn catalog, and NOTHING refuses. A port that refused every x-lvariant tag fails here.
CONTROL isolating the OTHER conjunct. The walk exhausts exactly as it does for en-US-x-lvariant-POSIX and answers the fallback; exhaustion alone is not what refuses.
CONTROL. A one-element attempted chain on the same fixture, so a port that refused on the fixture rather than on the chain fails here.

CONTROL against OVERCORRECTION, and the sharpest one here. The identical tag on the identical fixture answers the SELECTION channel without refusing, so a port that fixed the refusal at the tag layer (normalizeTag, or the request boundary) rather than in the resolution walk turns this row red while turning the getResult row green.
The paired control for the duplicate refusal: same request tag, a catalog that serves at 'en', and the colliding candidate is never reached. A port that refuses this tag unconditionally fails here.

The paired control for the ja refusal. Note the attempted chain still BEGINS with the legacy ja_JP_JP compatibility locale and that one is well-formed to Locale.Builder; only the lowercased candidate further down is not, and the walk stops at 'ja' before reaching it.
The paired control for the th refusal.
CONTROL. The bridge tag against a fixture with no Norwegian catalog at all: the walk runs nn-NO, nn, no and then the fallback, and still refuses nothing.
